A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the substantial replacement of the central theorem and proof.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical results, proofs and illustrative algebraic examples, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. Its new counterexample and Jacobian examples are mathematical constructions, not empirical results.

M1.justification: The feedforward PNN/hPNN models, monomial activations and homogenization construction are retained. The revisions change their theoretical guarantees rather than network architecture, training or inference procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or evaluated tasks. Changes to admissible network widths and degrees concern theoretical architecture conditions, not empirical coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed algorithm. Comparisons with previous identifiability bounds are theoretical.

E3.justification: Neither PDF specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. Revised degree and width conditions are mathematical assumptions, not experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness tests or empirical case studies. The new algebraic examples and counterexample support theoretical arguments assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are reported in either version. Changes to analytical bounds and symbolic examples are theoretical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 11 changes from parameter-wise uniqueness iff adjacent blocks are unique to a sufficient generic finite-identifiability theorem using minimum preceding layer widths. Appendix B replaces the tensor-lifting argument with composite-Jacobian rank lemmas and induction; Example 41 contradicts v1's uniqueness implication. Bottleneck conditions and bias-case proofs are revised. The stated universal activation bound changes from 2d_l - 2 in v1 Corollary 22 to 2d_l - 1 in v2 Corollary 17, which also allows a single output.

C1.justification: Sections 1.1 and 5 replace the claimed shallow-to-deep equivalence for global identifiability with a sufficient finite-identifiability result requiring restricted input counts. The claim of certifying uniqueness of given deep-network weights is withdrawn. Contributions concerning neurovariety dimensions and linear activation thresholds remain, under the revised guarantees.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 explicitly acknowledges that the techniques establish only finite identifiability for deep networks and leaves generic global identifiability as Conjecture 40. It explains that composing unique shallow networks need not preserve uniqueness. Section 3.2 also explains how the bottleneck width constrains the entire decoder, replacing the earlier emphasis on successive width increases.

D1.justification: Neither version provides an implemented training procedure, experimental hyperparameters, hardware details or code/data access instructions. Expanded proof constructions do not add implementation or reproducibility information of this kind.

R1.justification: The central positioning changes from claiming global uniqueness beyond prior work characterized as only locally identifiable to extending finite-identifiability theory for deep feedforward PNNs. Section 1 now acknowledges global-identifiability results for previously studied architectures. Additional references address PNN singularities, model merging and connections between finite and global identifiability.

P1.justification: The exposition is extensively revised around finite versus global identifiability. Section 4 is reorganized into necessary conditions, tensor tools and the main proof. The former omnibus proof Appendix A is reorganized into topical Appendices A-C, while the neurovariety and truncation appendices move to D and E.

P2.justification: v1's Figure 1 in Appendix A.4, illustrating three two-layer network architectures, is removed without a replacement figure. The single-column format remains, with reference and appendix material reflowed.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses a central correctness problem: Example 41 directly contradicts v1's Theorem 11. It replaces that assertion and its proof with a qualified finite-identifiability theorem and detailed Jacobian analysis in Appendix B. Although the guarantees are narrower and generic global identifiability becomes a conjecture, correcting the foundational claim substantially improves the paper's rigor and reliability.
